faqs.q: How many hours should a student study in a day?
faqs.a: There is no single right number; it depends on your class, your exams and how well you focus. A few hours of focused study with regular breaks usually achieves more than a long day of distracted reading, so build up your study time gradually and judge it by what you have learnt rather than by the clock.

faqs.q: How can I stop feeling sleepy while studying?
faqs.a: Get enough sleep at night, study at a desk in good light rather than on your bed, and take short breaks to stand up, stretch or walk. Drinking water and avoiding very heavy meals before a session also helps. If you feel tired all the time despite sleeping well, it is worth seeing a doctor.

faqs.q: How can I improve my concentration while studying?
faqs.a: Remove distractions first: keep your phone in another room or on silent and block distracting websites. Then work in timed blocks, such as 25 minutes of study followed by a 5-minute break, and set a clear goal for each block. Active methods like summarising in your own words keep your mind engaged.

faqs.q: How can I remember what I study for longer?
faqs.a: Test yourself instead of only re-reading. Try recalling key points from memory, using flashcards or explaining a topic aloud as if teaching someone, then revise the same material again after a few days. Spreading revision over time and sleeping well both help the brain hold on to what you have learnt.
